children: NeoVolta reported fiscal year 2026 revenue of $13.3 million, a 58% increase year-over-year, and a GAAP net loss of $21.5 million (or $(0.55) per share). The company disclosed fourth-quarter revenue of $13.5 thousand and a fourth-quarter GAAP net loss of $11.7 million, driven in part by credit loss provisions and inventory obsolescence reserves. NeoVolta also introduced Adjusted EBITDA as a supplemental non-GAAP measure, reporting Adjusted EBITDA of $(12.8) million for fiscal 2026.
Fiscal year 2026 revenue: $13.3 million, up 58% from $8.4 million in fiscal 2025.
Fourth quarter revenue: $13.5 thousand, compared with $4.8 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.
GAAP net loss for fiscal year 2026: $21.5 million, or $(0.55) per share; fiscal year 2025 net loss: $5.0 million, or $(0.15) per share.
Fourth-quarter GAAP net loss: $11.7 million, compared with $1.6 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP): $(12.8) million for fiscal year 2026; fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA: $(8.0) million.
Launched NeoVolta Power, the company's 80%-owned Pendergrass, Georgia utility and C&I scale energy storage manufacturing joint venture.

Received formal opinion confirming Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) compliance for the Pendergrass facility, the NVApex 5MWh BESS and the NVWave residential product, supporting IRA Section 48E eligibility.

Expanded commercial pipeline into utility-scale and C&I markets, including a non-binding LOI with Infinite Grid Capital for ~1.1 GWh and a binding capacity reservation for North Ontario Edge AI datacenter projects for 2027.

Announced a five-year strategic supply and manufacturing collaboration with SK On (announced August 31, 2026) including a signed agreement for SK On to supply 9 GWh of U.S.-manufactured LFP cells from 2027–2031 and a broader framework potentially supporting up to 18 GWh of combined activity.

Pendergrass facility progressing through commissioning with production ramp targeted to begin in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 and plans to pursue a second production line to scale capacity toward 8 GWh annually by calendar 2028.
